October 18, 2026

Trump pressures Kyiv as Zelensky warns against US siding with Russia

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

President Zelensky said Russia has struck Ukraine's energy, oil and gas infrastructure 76 times since Trump announced an energy ceasefire on Oct. 11, including nearly 2,700 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, with 11 people killed in the 24 hours to Sunday morning. In a Truth Social post, Trump said he would delay signing Russia sanctions legislation to avoid driving Moscow from the bargaining table, praised Russia for doing little to help Iran, and accused Zelensky of targeting Russian diesel refineries and of never wanting to end the war. Trump waived Graham Act sanctions on Friday and lifted the embargo on Russian diesel, drawing bipartisan criticism in Congress. Zelensky, speaking on NBC's Meet the Press, called the prospect of the United States siding with Russia a "historic mistake," said he had spoken with envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and said US intelligence sharing for missile defense had resumed after a brief pause.

Pentagon said to withhold Iran school strike investigation until after midterms

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Pentagon officials plan to hold the internal investigation into the Feb. 28 US strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in Minab, Iran, until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to Bloomberg News. Advisers to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told staff the report has been effectively finished for months; it blames flawed intelligence, outdated imagery and an overreliance on AI targeting systems for the Tomahawk strike, which killed more than 150 people, most of them children. A Pentagon official said the investigation remains ongoing and no release date is final. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand called the delay "disgraceful" and "cowardly," and the school was reportedly still listed as a Revolutionary Guard compound in an outdated targeting database.

Trump issues full endorsement of Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a Truth Social post on Sunday, urging voters to back him and the Likud party in the Oct. 27 legislative elections. He called Netanyahu "a Great Warrior Prime Minister" and a partner in combating Iran, said Iran had been systematically destroyed militarily and financially and that "we will soon finish the job," and wrote that if Israel elected anyone else "America will have to do this work ourselves." The endorsement ends weeks in which Trump declined to say whether Netanyahu deserved another term. Netanyahu faces corruption scandals, backlash over security failures before the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack, an International Criminal Court arrest warrant, and a challenge from former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot.

Ukraine strikes St Petersburg oil terminal and data center in mass drone attack

tags: war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks of the year overnight, hitting an oil terminal in St. Petersburg along with an Ozon logistics hub and a VKontakte data center. Russia's defense ministry said air defenses shot down 1,015 drones across 15 regions, and local authorities reported at least one person killed and several wounded. The strike came in defiance of Trump's demand that Kyiv stop hitting Russian energy infrastructure and deepens the collapse of the energy ceasefire he announced last week.

Romanian F-16s down two drones over Black Sea waters

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two drones over the country's territorial waters on Saturday, the defence ministry said. Defence Minister Radu Miruta said the drones were likely Russian-made Geran-4s, a new generation flying at about 450 km/h, and that it was the first time Romania had downed drones of that type. The shootdowns followed strikes on two chemical tankers near Romania's Black Sea coast, with seven crew members still missing; at least five other cargo ships have been hit near Romania and Bulgaria in the past two weeks, leaving 23 sailors dead or missing. Romania's foreign minister said the North Atlantic Council will meet Tuesday on Black Sea defence and deterrence.

Rubio says Ukraine does not have access to Starshield

tags: war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Ukraine does not currently have access to Starshield, drawing a distinction between Starlink as a commercial product and Starshield as a military and defense product used by the US military. He said the question of how Ukraine would use the system is under discussion. The remarks contradict administration claims that Ukraine has access to the capability.

Vance confronted at town hall by widower of soldier killed in Iran

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

Vice President JD Vance was confronted at a town hall by Joey Amor, whose wife, Master Sgt. Nicole Amor, was killed alongside five other soldiers in an Iranian drone strike on March 1, 2026. Amor said there were fundamental failures and leadership failures that led to the deaths, that other soldiers know things they are staying quiet about, and asked how the administration would hold leaders accountable. Vance said the country owed the family a debt it could not repay, said it was the first he had heard of the alleged failures, and promised to continue the conversation offline and find out what went wrong.

Golf course announcement collides with Trump administration's court filings

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump announced plans, under the Interior Secretary, for a new golf course at East Potomac Park in Washington, DC, a project expected to take more than 12 months, while trees at the park are already being cleared and a federal judge has urged the administration to stop. The Justice Department had told the court that Trump had no final plan to redevelop the park. The issue was compounded when outgoing White House press secretary Katie Zacharia posted a photograph showing a map of the site, then posted an apparently altered version of an image taken the same night with the map removed. The judge has questioned whether the government's position still stands, ordered concrete plans released, and summoned the Justice Department's third-ranking official, Stanley Woodward, to court over a potential disqualification.

Putin envoy says US and Russia discussing nuclear-powered data center projects

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Kirill Dmitriev, a top ally of Vladimir Putin, said the United States and Russia are discussing joint projects including US data centers running on Russian nuclear power, according to Reuters. Dmitriev said Trump and Putin are discussing a wide range of projects and that important initiatives would be announced in the near future.

India tells nationals in Saudi Arabia to follow emergency directives after Houthi strikes

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

India's embassy in Riyadh urged its nationals in Saudi Arabia to follow updated Saudi emergency directives amid heightened security concerns following Houthi drone and missile strikes. The advisory tells people to shelter in an interior room away from windows when an alert sounds, to stay off balconies and rooftops, and tells drivers to pull over away from bridges and tall buildings. The directives follow a wave of strikes by Iran-based Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport that killed 13 people, according to the Saudi-led coalition.

Bukele plans to release up to half of those jailed in El Salvador crackdown

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

President Nayib Bukele announced plans to release up to half of the more than 90,000 people arrested under the state of emergency in place since March 2022, focusing on those accused of collaborating with gangs, including lookouts and people who paid extortion. Authorities would review individual cases and consider early release under monitoring, though no timeline was given, and the emergency measures suspending access to legal counsel and other rights would remain. Human rights groups have documented more than 6,000 complaints and at least 575 deaths in custody, while government figures show homicides fell to 1.3 per 100,000 residents in 2025.

Microsoft president says AI faces fewer safety rules than milk or washing machines

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews

Microsoft President Brad Smith told the BBC that artificial intelligence is subject to fewer safety regulations than milk or washing machines and called for government oversight, arguing industry self-regulation is insufficient. He proposed requiring safety mechanisms capable of halting AI systems and laws compelling companies to notify victims of AI-related security breaches, comparing the protections to emergency brakes on trains and aircraft safety certification. Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and Nvidia signed a White House agreement in September committing to AI safety measures.

Republican advisers say Trump's remarks are crowding out affordability message

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

With about two weeks until the midterm elections, Republican advisers have questioned Trump's repeated comments praising the physical appearance of men, including Republican senators and football players, according to The New York Times. Advisers say the remarks are detracting from the party's affordability message in the final stretch of the campaign.

Texts show ousted press secretary sought the Fox News hits that ended her tenure

tags: politics, media
sources: @oafnation_actual

Text messages obtained by the New York Post show former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia personally pushed for the Fox News appearances that preceded the end of her five-day tenure, writing that she would like to do news hits morning and evening. In interviews with Sean Hannity and "Fox & Friends," she struggled to explain her failure to pass the California bar and to go beyond talking points. The texts undercut a Politico report describing the bookings as a "sanctioned hit" orchestrated by Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, who had not signed off on the hiring; the White House called those claims a smear. Trump said publicly on Friday that Zacharia was not right for the role.

Norte Fire reaches 25% containment as Orange County evacuations lift

tags: climate
sources: @oafnation_actual

Firefighters reached 25% containment on the Norte Fire in south Orange County and most evacuation orders were lifted Saturday evening, according to the Orange County Fire Authority and Cal Fire. Roughly 16,000 residents of San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano can return home after the fire, which broke out Friday near San Clemente, burned 570 acres and damaged or destroyed at least six homes as Santa Ana winds pushed it through hillside neighborhoods. Two firefighters were hospitalized with heat-related injuries. It is one of about 10 uncontained wildfires burning across California, and crews warn that embers and hot spots still pose a rekindle risk.
